title: CPAT-AI: Rebuilding a Policy Model
subtitle: Two AI-assisted rebuilds of the Climate Policy Assessment Tool, and what they found
message: Rebuilt twice in October 2026, as code-written Excel and as Python, under one rule (fix bugs, copy and track issues), legacy CPAT turned out to hold 228 bugs, 24 of high priority. Writing it a second time found seven bugs in the first rebuild.

problem.title: A model nobody could audit

stats.label: legacy workbook; main sheet past row 18,000
issues: intended choices open to question

problem.text: Formulas differed from row to row, constants were typed into formulas and the documentation had drifted from the workbook. Egypt's population followed a misread path; a one-off GDP effect compounded every year; a methane fee on farming and waste did nothing.

mechanism.title: One register, shared codes, tests on every output
mechanism.caption: CPAT-AI register, release 1.0.2 (29 October 2026).
points: Bugs are never replicated; issues are replicated and tracked.
One code per variable in legacy, Excel-AI and Coded CPAT: comparison is a table join.
Coded CPAT matches Excel-AI on 7,458 output codes within 10⁻⁹.
Built with Claude Code and GitHub Copilot; every judgment kept by the owner.

action.title: Build policy models twice
results: The CPAT team confirmed 52 fixes; 2 marked fixed were not.
Verification is not validation: three agreeing models can share a wrong assumption.
Air pollution and transport co-benefits are not yet rebuilt.
todo: Require a codes map as a model deliverable.
Keep one register of bugs, issues, departures and upgrades.
Build twice and regression-test every release.
Use AI agents as builders under written norms, not as authorities.
